rules.statement: Redeem single-use shared state (such as a login transaction or one-time code) with one atomic take operation, such as `GETDEL`, rather than a read followed by a separate remove.
rules.why: The callback that redeems it has to remove it atomically, so a replayed or concurrent callback finds nothing and the state is never redeemed twice.
rules.check: Look for code that consumes one-time state with a Get followed by a Remove/Delete, or any non-atomic check-then-delete on a shared store.

rules.statement: Update shared state that concurrent requests may modify by compare-and-swap on a version, and handle a failed swap, rather than overwriting it blindly.
rules.why: Two concurrent requests that refresh the same entry, such as a session's tokens, must not overwrite each other's writes.
rules.check: Look for read-modify-write of a shared session or entry that ends in an unconditional Set/Replace with no expected version, or that ignores the result of a conditional replace.

rules.statement: Do not use `IDistributedCache` for shared state that needs atomic add-if-absent, take or compare-and-swap semantics.
rules.why: `IDistributedCache` has no atomic add, take or compare-and-swap, so state could be redeemed twice and concurrent updates could overwrite each other.
rules.check: Look for `IDistributedCache` used to store login transactions, sessions, nonces or other single-use or concurrently updated state.

rules.statement: In an in-memory store, copy a caller's byte buffer (`ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` or array) on write instead of keeping a reference to it.
rules.why: A caller that reuses its buffer must not be able to change an entry that is already stored.
rules.check: Look for in-process stores or caches that keep a passed-in `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>`/`byte[]` directly, with no `.ToArray()` or other copy.

rules.statement: Let shared-state store failures throw so the caller fails closed, and never treat a read that failed as the entry being absent.
rules.why: A session or security state that cannot be read must not be treated as missing; the caller fails closed (for example by returning 503).
rules.check: Look for catch blocks around store calls that swallow the exception and return null, false or empty, or that treat the failure as 'not found'.

rules.statement: In Valkey/Redis, put any compare-then-write or multi-step update (prune plus TTL extension, version check plus set) in one server-side Lua script, or use a single atomic command such as `SET NX PX` or `GETDEL`.
rules.why: The comparison and the write then happen atomically on the server, so concurrent replicas cannot interleave between them.
rules.check: Look for Valkey/Redis code that issues a GET followed by a separate SET/EXPIRE/ZADD that depends on the value it read, with no script or transaction around them.

rules.statement: Make sure shared-store keys that collect members (sets, sorted sets, indexes) are bounded: prune expired members and keep the key's TTL no longer than its longest-lived member.
rules.why: An index must live no longer than the longest time-to-live applied to it and must never grow without bound.
rules.check: Look for code that adds members to a Valkey/Redis set or sorted set with no pruning of expired members and no TTL on the key.

rules.statement: Encrypt values before writing them to a shared external store when they must not be readable there; the store treats values as opaque bytes and does not protect them.
rules.why: The store keeps opaque bytes, so the caller serializes values and encrypts whatever must not be readable in the store.
rules.check: Look for tokens, secrets or session contents serialized and written to a shared store without being encrypted or data-protected first.
